summary: Added optional inbound --admin-api-key protection for the experimental Rust router's POST /flush_cache endpoint. With no key configured the existing unauthenticated behavior is preserved. With a key configured, only an exact Authorization: Bearer <key> credential is accepted, unauthorized requests return 401 before worker registry access/fan-out, and the inbound credential is not forwarded to workers.

tests.what_was_measured: Baseline reproduction on the recorded base: the existing no-key POST /flush_cache path contacted two real local HTTP fake workers and returned success, confirming the reported unauthenticated behavior. Raw output: reports/j-7d06fd1a3a2a/raw/before_existing_unauthenticated_fanout.log

Nine cache-route tests, including backward-compatible no-key fan-out, exact bearer success, missing/wrong scheme/wrong key rejection, zero worker calls for all unauthorized requests, and no forwarding of the inbound Authorization header. Raw output: reports/j-7d06fd1a3a2a/raw/after_cache_auth_tests.log

Complete router test suite: 549 library tests, 4 binary tests, 58 component tests, and 90 proxy tests passed. This includes CLI parsing and rejection of empty/header-invalid admin keys. Raw output: reports/j-7d06fd1a3a2a/raw/full_cargo_test.log
All modified Rust source conforms to the pinned rustfmt. Raw output: reports/j-7d06fd1a3a2a/raw/cargo_fmt_check.log
